meta.goal: Field decision (Oct 15) + artifacts + fluency baseline for ThinkSwiss outreach (Nov waves, letter by Dec 20, application by Jan 15 2027)
meta.definition_of_done_per_ticket: code_proof passes AND closed-book reconstruction_gate passes on paper. Deadlines are scheduling aids, NEVER completion criteria. A ticket closed at recognition-depth is a failed ticket with a checkmark.

daily_template.theory_block: 14:00-15:30, pen and paper, peak cognition window
daily_template.verification_block: 15:30-16:15, NumPy/PyTorch adversarial check of the day's theory
daily_template.decode_rep: 20 min, 4x/week, one equation block from a real paper, from Phase B onward
daily_template.struggle_timer_ladder: 20 min (Jul 15-21), 30 min (Jul 22 - Aug 4), 45 min (Aug 5 onward, permanent)

rules.frustration_spike: Topic-switching and YouTube are BANNED mid-timer. A walk is legal only after writing one hypothesis-stack line stating the exact stall point; max 10 min; return to the same line.
rules.ai_usage: AI never explains first. You derive/decode/translate first; AI checks, attacks, and quizzes after. Hint ladders only when the timer expires.
rules.training_runs: When a run diverges: write a one-line diagnosis (logic bug vs hyperparameter collapse) BEFORE touching anything, then test that hypothesis.
rules.compute: Local GTX 1650 first. Kaggle free GPU (~30 hrs/week) for overflow batch runs only — notebooks are for training, never for exploratory procrastination. No paid cloud.
banned_this_window: EBM/statistical-physics deep dive (deferred until a target lab demands it)

phases.name: Foundation rebuild
phases.note: Highest-capacity 3.5 weeks (pre-semester). Two parallel tracks: linear algebra + matrix calculus; probability from the true beginning.

subtopics: matrices as linear maps: what they DO to space
column space, rank, null space
eigenvectors/eigenvalues: geometric meaning before computation
symmetric (A = A^T) vs orthogonal (A A^T = I) — the exact confusion from probe 1, separated permanently
spectral theorem for symmetric matrices: real eigenvalues, orthogonal eigenvectors
SVD as rotate-scale-rotate; A^T A has no negative eigenvalues (probe 5)
resources: 3Blue1Brown, Essence of Linear Algebra, episodes 1-10 (geometric layer)
MIT 18.06 (Strang): lectures 1-8, 21-22
Trefethen & Bau lectures 4-5 (SVD) as the capstone read
tickets.code_proof: NumPy: apply a symmetric, an orthogonal, and a generic 2x2 matrix to the unit circle and plot all three; verify spectral theorem numerically on a random symmetric matrix; construct A with rank deficiency and show what SVD reveals that eigendecomposition cannot.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Closed book: state spectral theorem precisely; prove A^T A is PSD in 3 lines; explain symmetric-vs-orthogonal to a rubber duck without conflation.

subtopics: scalar-by-vector and scalar-by-matrix gradients; shape discipline (write every shape)
Jacobians; the vector chain rule
grad of x^T A x (general and symmetric A) — probe 1 retaken properly
grad_W ||XW - y||^2 — probe 2 retaken properly
grad of softmax + cross-entropy composite
finite-difference verification as a permanent habit
resources: Parr & Howard, 'The Matrix Calculus You Need For Deep Learning' — FULL, every identity re-derived on paper before turning the page. This paper defeated you once; it is now both curriculum and calibration instrument.
tickets.code_proof: Hand-derive then finite-difference-check (5 random points each): grad x^T A x, grad_W ||XW - y||^2, grad of 2-layer MLP loss w.r.t. both weight matrices. Checks must include one near-boundary/ill-conditioned point.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Closed book: probes 1 and 2 from the diagnostic, full derivations with shapes annotated, under 25 minutes combined.

subtopics: sample space, events, axioms; conditioning and Bayes (your strength — keep it)
random variable as a FUNCTION on outcomes — not 'a probability' (probe 3 repair)
the type system: RV vs distribution vs density vs probability — four different objects
PMF/PDF/CDF; why a density can exceed 1 but never go negative (probe 6 repair)
law of total probability; independence
resources: Blitzstein & Hwang, Introduction to Probability, ch 1-3, 5
Harvard Stat 110 lectures paired to those chapters
tickets.code_proof: Simulate a 2-coin sample space explicitly as outcomes; implement an RV as a literal Python function on outcomes; recover its distribution by counting; plot a Beta(0.5,0.5) density and mark where it exceeds 1.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Closed book: probe 3 retaken — define RV formally, explain E[X] for continuous X as a weighted average (meaning, not formula), and give the four-object type table from memory.

subtopics: expectation as probability-weighted average; LOTUS
linearity of expectation (and why it needs no independence)
variance, covariance intro
indicator-variable trick
an RV whose expectation does not exist (Cauchy / St. Petersburg) — and what diverging Monte Carlo looks like
resources: Blitzstein & Hwang ch 4 + expectation sections of ch 5-6
Stat 110 corresponding lectures
tickets.code_proof: Monte Carlo E[g(X)] for a nonlinear g two ways (sampling vs numeric integral) and show agreement; simulate Cauchy sample means at n = 10^2..10^6 and show non-convergence; verify Jensen's inequality numerically for a convex g.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Closed book: state and prove linearity of expectation for the discrete case; explain in one paragraph why E[f(X)] != f(E[X]) in general and name the inequality that governs the convex case.

tickets.topic: MILESTONE — MNIST training loop from a blank file
subtopics: Dataset/DataLoader, transform, batching
model definition, forward
cross-entropy loss, backward, optimizer step
train/eval split discipline, accuracy reporting
resources: None. That is the point. No reference, no AI, no video.
tickets.code_proof: A working MNIST classifier written cold from an empty file, >95% test accuracy, plus a one-paragraph note on every place you got stuck and how you got out.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: The artifact IS the gate. Converts 'PyTorch' on the resume from claim to fact.

phases.exit_exam: Closed book, on paper, timed: diagnostic probes 1, 2, 3, 5 — the four you failed on July 12. Beating your own diagnostic is the proof of motion. Send the wreckage either way.

phases.name: Collision phase — semester running
phases.note: Volume drops by design, not surrender. The 14:00-16:30 block survives everything; GSoC in the morning; classes get the remainder. Decode rep (20 min, 4x/week) starts here.

tickets.topic: Probability II — joint structure and conditioning
subtopics: joint, marginal, conditional distributions
covariance and correlation; what correlation does NOT tell you
conditional expectation as a random variable; tower property
multivariate Gaussian: reading Sigma geometrically
resources: Blitzstein & Hwang ch 7-9
Stat 110 corresponding lectures
tickets.code_proof: Sample correlated Gaussians via Cholesky; verify tower property numerically on a hierarchical model; plot conditional distributions of a 2D Gaussian and show how the conditional mean is a linear function.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Closed book: derive the tower property; explain 'conditional expectation is a random variable' to a rubber duck with a concrete two-stage example.

subtopics: entropy; cross-entropy as THE classification loss (connect to A5's loss line)
KL divergence: definition, asymmetry, KL >= 0 via Jensen
absolute continuity: exactly when KL is infinite (probe 6, answered properly this time)
mutual information, first pass
resources: Cover & Thomas ch 2
MacKay ITILA ch 1-2 for intuition
tickets.code_proof: Compute KL between two Gaussians in closed form AND by Monte Carlo, show agreement; construct p, q where KL(p||q) is finite but KL(q||p) diverges, demonstrate numerically; implement cross-entropy from raw logits and match torch.nn.functional to 1e-6.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Closed book: prove KL >= 0; state the absolute-continuity condition and give the concrete infinite-KL example; explain KL asymmetry with the mode-seeking vs mass-covering picture.

subtopics: every gradient in a 2-layer network derived by hand, end to end
backprop as the vector chain rule organized efficiently — nothing more
resources: Your own A2 notes. No new material.
tickets.code_proof: NumPy-only 2-layer network on a toy dataset: forward and manual backward from your derivations, gradients matched against finite differences AND against a PyTorch autograd twin.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Closed book: full backward pass derivation for the 2-layer net, shapes annotated, one sitting.

subtopics: Value node with grad; backward closures; topological sort; broadcasting-free scalar autograd
the right-sized answer to the 'how does PyTorch work' itch — 10-414 stays banned
resources: None during the build. You typed along with Karpathy once; producing it cold is the ownership version.
tickets.code_proof: From a blank file, no reference: scalar autograd engine + tiny MLP that learns XOR. Then and only then, diff against Karpathy's repo and write 5 lines on what you structured differently and why.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: The artifact is the gate. 2-3 sessions maximum — if it is eating more, stop and report, do not grind silently.

subtopics: Moving MNIST next-frame prediction: a genuine tiny world model on a 1650
sequence Dataset/DataLoader (research-infrastructure skill, learned by necessity)
loss-curve reading; divergence diagnosis discipline (logic bug vs hyperparameter, hypothesis written before touching anything)
checkpointing and a clean eval script
resources: Moving MNIST dataset (public)
PyTorch docs as reference (reference use is legal; generation is yours)
tickets.deadline: 2026-09-14 for first end-to-end run; trial continues into Phase C
tickets.code_proof: A conv encoder-decoder (or ConvLSTM if it earns its complexity) predicting frame t+1 from context frames, trained locally or on Kaggle overflow, with saved checkpoints, a loss curve, and a 5-line training log per run including the pre-edit divergence hypothesis where applicable.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Daily tastelog line (drift/dread/one-liner) from Sep 1 onward — the log IS the deliverable; enjoyment is not the metric, voluntary return is.

phases.exit_exam: B2 and B3 reconstruction gates passed; MNIST milestone artifact exists; tastelog has >= 14 consecutive daily entries.

phases.name: Convergence — trial, scouting, first solo paper
phases.note: Theory drops to maintenance (45 min/day). The month belongs to the trial arms, the pipeline, and the I-JEPA read.

subtopics: fixed evaluation protocol: same data split, same metrics (MSE + one perceptual/structural metric), same context length, for every model
your B5 model vs one public implementation, compared honestly
one ablation each (e.g., context length, latent size) — the researcher's move installed as habit
error analysis: where do both fail, and differently?
resources: One public Moving-MNIST prediction repo of your choosing (reading foreign research code is itself the skill)
tickets.code_proof: An evaluation harness (config-driven, seeded, deterministic eval) producing one comparison table + one ablation table, and an 800-word writeup with the tables. This artifact anchors every November cold email.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: The writeup must contain at least one sentence of the form 'X did not matter, and here is the evidence' — a real ablation finding, not a summary.

subtopics: arxiv_scout runs Tue/Fri, 2 professors per session, from Sep 15
labs.csv human columns filled same session (hosts-visitors evidence, code-publishing, fit 1-5)
target: >= 18 scored rows by Oct 15, top-5 shortlist drafted
resources: pipeline/arxiv_scout.py + labs.csv (already built)
tickets.code_proof: labs.csv with >= 18 fully-scored rows; a shortlist note naming top 5 labs with one sentence each on WHY (signal overlap, not prestige).
tickets.reconstruction_gate: None — this is operations. The discipline is the twice-weekly cadence, not depth.

tickets.topic: MILESTONE — I-JEPA read solo, start to finish
subtopics: full decode protocol per equation block: symbol table, types, plain sentence, instantiation, ancestor
no AI, no video, no blog explainers — first complete solo paper read of your life, timed for when the vocabulary exists
glossary rows appended per session
resources: arXiv:2301.08243 (I-JEPA). Sessions of 45-60 min; expect 5-8 sessions; speed is not the metric.
tickets.code_proof: Complete notation glossary for the paper; one 20-line NumPy instantiation of the core loss on toy tensors; a half-page 'what I could not resolve' list (an honest unresolved list is a PASS, a suspiciously empty one is a FAIL).
tickets.reconstruction_gate: Closed book: write the I-JEPA objective from memory with every symbol typed, then explain aloud (recorded, 3 min) what is predicted, in what space, and why not pixel space.

subtopics: evidence: tastelog verdict (drift/dread/abort tallies), both trial artifacts, scouting shortlist
decision: training-flavored vs evaluation-flavored empirical work (or the fused identity if the evidence splits)
output: one paragraph naming the field + the Phase-3 niche module it selects + the 3 labs wave-1 outreach targets first
resources: Your own logs. No external opinions. The decision is made from data, by you, in one sitting.
tickets.code_proof: The decision paragraph, written and dated.
tickets.reconstruction_gate: None. This ticket closes the 90 days and opens the outreach phase.

phases.exit_exam: C1 writeup exists, C3 glossary exists, C4 paragraph written. These three artifacts + labs.csv are the complete input to November.
